full_judgment:
4. The trial Court decreed the instant suit for eviction by its judgment and decree passed on July 27, 1981 on the finding that relationship of landlord and tenant exists between the parties on the basis of a firisti showing filing of a case under section 107 CrPC against the plaintiff respondents, the appellants admitting themselves to be monthly tenants under them and also on the basis of a letter written by them requesting the plaintiff-respondents for repairing some part of the rented house. The firisti was relied upon as the documents shown in the firisti along with other documents kept in the safe custody of the court were found missing. The defendant-appellants preferred other Appeal No.123 of 1981 against the judgment and decree of the trial Court. The lower appellate Court by its judgment and decree on April 26, 1982 allowed the appeal, set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and dismissed the suit on the finding that the plaintiff-respondents failed to establish existence of relationship of landlord and tenant. 

 5. The plaintiff-respondents against the judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court preferred an application under section 115 CPC and obtained a Rule in the aforementioned Civil Revision Case. The learned Single Judge on contest concurring with the finding of the trial Court on existence of relationship of landlord and tenants relying upon Ext. 1, the firisti, set aside the judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court, made the Rule absolute and decreed the suit. 

 7. Mr. Mansur Habib, the learned Advocate for the defendant-appellants, submitted that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division was wrong in holding that relationship of landlord and tenant between the parties exists merely relying upon the firisti, Ext. 1 and illegally interfered with the decision of the lower appellate Court and decreed the suit. He contended that a certified copy of a firisti showing filing of documents, here in this instant case, copy of criminal proceeding under section 107 CrPC and letters written by the defendants to plaintiff No. 1 to repair the house, cannot be held to be evidence to prove relationship of landlord and tenant in respect of the present premises in suit. Firisti is a list showing therein entry of the documents to be adduced as evidence in a particular case and it is not the evidence of the contents of the documents. As no evidence has been adduced by the plaintiffs to prove relationship of landlord and tenant between the defendant- appellants and the plaintiff-respondents the learned Single Judge erroneously arrived at a finding on the existence of such relationship merely on the basis of a certified copy of a firisti which is no evidence. 

 11. For the aforesaid reasons, we set aside the judgment and decree of the learned Judge of the High Court Division and dismiss the suit.
